paper_records.paper_title: Hysteresis of Multiconfiguration Assemblies of Nitinol and Steel Strands: Experiments and Phenomenological Identification
paper_records.why_added: Core prior art paper on cyclic hysteresis of multi-configuration assemblies of Nitinol and steel strands.
paper_records.threat_addressed: Central paper for T1 and T3; historically linked to CONTRA-03 (S2a steel vs S1a NiTi misattribution).
paper_records.method: Experimental dynamic testing and phenomenological hysteresis identification
paper_records.material_or_system: Multiconfiguration strand assemblies: Specimen S1a (NiTi7 strand) and Specimen S2a (ST49 steel wire rope)
paper_records.loading_mode: Cyclic tension and combined tension-bending flexure
paper_records.control_variables: Displacement amplitude, tension preload, excitation frequency (0.1 to 2 Hz)
paper_records.independent_variables: Specimen configuration (S1a NiTi7 vs S2a steel ST49), pretension level (1.5 kN to 4.5 kN), cyclic flexural displacement
paper_records.dependent_variables: Force-displacement hysteresis loops, equivalent stiffness, dissipated energy, Bouc-Wen model parameters
paper_records.constitutive_model: Graesser-type superelastic formulation combined with Bouc-Wen friction damping
paper_records.contact_or_friction_model: Inter-wire friction dissipation captured via evolutionary differential variable
paper_records.experiment_used: MTS servo-hydraulic biaxial testing system with specialized bending-tension fixtures
paper_records.experimental_setup: Strand clamped under axial preload with transverse actuator applying cyclic lateral flexure
paper_records.key_results: Demonstrated that NiTi7 strand under tension-bending (S1a) exhibits combined friction and superelastic hysteresis; confirmed that specimen S2a was ST49 steel wire rope exhibiting pure friction hysteresis without phase transformation.
paper_records.what_it_proves: Proves that multiwire NiTi assemblies under cyclic flexure dissipate energy via simultaneous inter-wire friction and pseudoelasticity (in configuration S1a).
paper_records.what_it_does_not_prove: Did NOT test pure cyclic bending of NiTi without tension preload; did NOT test specimen S2a as NiTi (S2a was steel).
directly_verified_statements: Specimen S1a is composed of a 1x7 NiTi strand tested under combined tension and flexure (Table 1, p. 3).
Specimen S2a is an ST49 high-strength steel wire rope tested under cyclic flexure (Table 1, p. 3; Table 4, p. 10).
Energy dissipation in S1a originates from both Coulomb friction and martensitic phase transformation (Section 5, pp. 8-11).
inferred_statements: Without an axial tensile preload, thin NiTi wire bundles may buckle on the compressive side during pure bending unless radial confinement is applied.
paper_records.limitations: S1a required substantial axial tension preload (1.5-4.5 kN); S2a was steel; no active fluid confinement pressure.
paper_records.impact_on_MP1: Direct focus of mandatory correction CONTRA-03: Stage 1 extraction error claiming S2a proved NiTi pure bending is completely expunged.
paper_records.evidence_pointers: Table 1 (specimen designations S1a vs S2a), Fig. 8 (S1a tension-bending hysteresis loops)
paper_records.metadata_conflicts: Often cited as 2014 in conference/online first, published in ASCE Journal of Engineering Mechanics in 2015.

paper_records.paper_title: Superelasticity SMA cables and its simplified FE model
paper_records.repository_path: data/papers/verification/MP1-V002/A2-2023-Superelasticity SMA cables and its simplified FE model.pdf
paper_records.matrix_filename: A2-2023-Superelasticity SMA cables and its simplified FE model.pdf
paper_records.why_added: Recent study proposing simplified finite element models for superelastic SMA cables.
paper_records.threat_addressed: Threatens model necessity by demonstrating efficient simplified FE modeling of NiTi cables.
paper_records.method: Theoretical simplification, 3D FE modeling, and experimental tension validation
paper_records.independent_variables: Cable structure, helical lay angle, number of cycles
paper_records.dependent_variables: Axial force-strain curve, computational efficiency, residual strain
paper_records.model_used: Simplified beam-truss model with equivalent cross-sectional parameters
paper_records.constitutive_model: Auricchio superelastic model implemented in ANSYS/Abaqus
paper_records.contact_or_friction_model: Coupled kinematic constraint representing inter-wire frictional resistance
paper_records.experiment_used: Tensile testing machine with digital extensometer
paper_records.experimental_setup: SMA cable specimens tested under uniaxial cyclic tension with displacement control
paper_records.key_results: Demonstrated that a simplified FE model using equivalent beam elements accurately predicts the superelastic behavior of NiTi cables while reducing computing time by over 90% compared to full 3D solid contact models.
paper_records.what_it_proves: Proves that simplified structural models can capture multiwire NiTi cable response accurately without full 3D contact discretization.
paper_records.what_it_does_not_prove: Does not examine lateral bending under variable transverse pressure.
directly_verified_statements: The simplified FE model reproduces cyclic tension curves with <5% error while reducing computational degrees of freedom by an order of magnitude (Section 3, pp. 5-8).
Axial stiffness degrades progressively during early loading cycles before stabilizing into a steady limit cycle (Section 4, pp. 9-11).
inferred_statements: Simplified structural models (H0b variants) can capture cable mechanics effectively for engineering control.
paper_records.limitations: Axial tension only; no lateral confinement pressure.
paper_records.impact_on_MP1: Reinforces H0b by showing that simplified structural models adequately describe NiTi cables.
paper_records.evidence_pointers: Fig. 5 (simplified model schematic), Fig. 9 (comparison of simplified vs 3D solid model)
